Ordinary Quarto text outside a `cr-section` scrolls as usual. Each section below
shows a different group of closeread features.

# 1. Highlighting and zooming (sidebar-left)

:::{.cr-section}

A **trigger** is any paragraph that contains `@cr-<id>`. When it scrolls into view,
the sticky with that id appears. @cr-poem

`highlight="1"` highlights a line by its number. [@cr-poem]{highlight="1"}

A range works too: `highlight="2-3"`. [@cr-poem]{highlight="2-3"}

You can also highlight a span you've tagged with an id, like
`[yellow wood]{#cr-wood}`. [@cr-poem]{highlight="cr-wood"}

`zoom-to="4"` zooms in on line 4 and centers it. [@cr-poem]{zoom-to="4"}

`hlz="5"` highlights and zooms in one step. [@cr-poem]{hlz="5"}

:::{#cr-poem}
| Two roads diverged in a [yellow wood]{#cr-wood},
| And sorry I could not travel both
| And be one traveler, long I stood
| And looked down one as far as I could
| To where it bent in the undergrowth;
:::

:::

# 2. Code as a sticky (sidebar-right)

:::{.cr-section layout="sidebar-right"}

Code blocks can be stickies too. This section uses `layout="sidebar-right"`. @cr-code

Code lines can be highlighted by number, just like poem lines. [@cr-code]{highlight="1-2"}

Here we highlight the loop body. [@cr-code]{highlight="5-6"}

A trigger can also be a whole div with `focus-on="cr-code"` instead of an inline `@cr-code`.
This is useful for longer passages with several paragraphs.

:::{focus-on="cr-code" highlight="8"}
This entire div is one trigger.

It highlights the `return` line.
:::

:::{#cr-code}
```python
def fizzbuzz(n):
    out = []
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        word = ""
        if i % 3 == 0: word += "Fizz"
        if i % 5 == 0: word += "Buzz"
        out.append(word or str(i))
    return out
```
:::

:::

# 3. Pan and scale (overlay-center)

:::{.cr-section layout="overlay-center"}

In overlay layouts, the text floats over a full-width sticky. @cr-map

`scale-by="2"` scales the sticky by a factor. [@cr-map]{scale-by="2"}

`pan-to` moves it with a CSS translate. Here it moves to the top-left corner.
[@cr-map]{pan-to="25%,25%" scale-by="2"}

And now to the bottom-right. [@cr-map]{pan-to="-25%,-25%" scale-by="2"}

Back to the full view. @cr-map

:::{#cr-map}
```{=html}
<svg viewBox="0 0 400 300" width="600" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <rect width="400" height="300" style="fill: var(--color-surface-hover); stroke: var(--color-border)"/>
  <circle cx="80"  cy="70"  r="40" style="fill: var(--color-accent)"/>
  <text   x="80"   y="75"  text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" style="fill: var(--color-on-accent)">top-left</text>
  <circle cx="320" cy="230" r="40" style="fill: var(--color-bg)"/>
  <text   x="320"  y="234" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" style="fill: var(--color-on-bg)">bottom-right</text>
  <rect x="160" y="120" width="80" height="60" style="fill: var(--color-signal)"/>
  <text x="200" y="155" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" style="fill: var(--color-on-accent)">center</text>
</svg>
```
:::

:::

# 4. Spacing, swapping stickies and live progress (overlay-left)

:::{.cr-section layout="overlay-left"}

Use the spacer shortcode to add scroll distance between triggers. @cr-box1

{{< spacer 60svh >}}

Point a trigger at a different id to swap stickies. @cr-box2

Add the `.scale-to-fill` class to a sticky to grow it to fill the space. @cr-box3

Closeread exposes scroll state to OJS. Variables include `crActiveSticky`,
`crTriggerIndex` and `crTriggerProgress`. Scroll slowly here. @cr-progress

:::{#cr-box1}
**Sticky one**: plain Markdown can be a sticky.
:::

:::{#cr-box2}
> **Sticky two**: so can a blockquote, table, image or figure.
:::

:::{#cr-box3 .scale-to-fill}
🌲
:::

:::{#cr-progress}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`**Active sticky:** ${crActiveSticky}

**Trigger index:** ${crTriggerIndex}

**Progress through this trigger:** ${Math.round(crTriggerProgress * 100)}%`
```
:::

:::

Text after the final section scrolls normally again. To see trigger and sticky
outlines while you build, set `debug-mode: true` in the header.
